title: Pasta con le Sarde
subtitle: sicilian pasta with sardines, fennel and sweet spices
excerpt: Pasta con le Sarde is Sicily's most celebrated pasta dish, combining fresh sardines with fennel, saffron, pine nuts and raisins in a sauce that balances sweet and savoury in equal measure. The technique is to cook the sardines gently and fold them through the fennel base so they stay in flakes rather than dissolving. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Pasta con le Sarde originated in Palermo and is considered the national dish of Sicily. Its combination of sweet and savoury ingredients traces directly to Arab influence on the island between the 9th and 11th centuries, when saffron, raisins and pine nuts first entered Sicilian kitchens.

content.text: Pasta con le Sarde pairs fresh sardines with wild fennel, saffron, pine nuts and raisins in a sauce built on the principle of

, where sweet raisins and sour-savoury fish create a flavour balance that is distinctly Sicilian. The key technique is cooking the sardines separately and folding them in at the end so they stay in large, soft flakes. This dish serves 4 and takes around 50 minutes from start to finish.
base of onion and fennel cooked slowly in olive oil. This gives the sauce its depth before any fish is added.
Bring a large pan of water to the boil. Add the fennel slices and cook for 5 minutes until just tender. Lift out with a slotted spoon and set aside. Keep the water on the heat for the pasta.
Season the cooking water and add your pasta. Bucatini or spaghetti work well. Cook until al dente according to packet instructions. Reserve a ladleful of pasta water before draining.

While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add the anchovy fillets and stir until they dissolve into the oil, about 2 minutes.
Add the cooked fennel, pine nuts and raisins. Pour in the saffron water and stir to combine. Cook for 3 minutes.

Lay the sardine fillets on top of the sauce. Cover with a lid and cook over medium-low heat for 4 minutes until just cooked through. Gently break the sardines into large flakes with a wooden spoon. Season to taste.
Add the drained pasta to the pan with a splash of reserved pasta water. Toss to coat, loosening with more pasta water if the sauce looks tight.
Divide between four bowls. Scatter the toasted breadcrumbs and the reserved fennel fronds over the top and serve straight away.

attrs.symptom: Sardines have broken down into mush
attrs.cause: They were added too early or stirred too hard once in the pan
attrs.fix: Add sardines at the very end, cover the pan and let them steam gently without stirring

attrs.symptom: Sauce tastes flat and lacks depth
attrs.cause: Anchovies were not fully melted or saffron was not dissolved properly
attrs.fix: Cook anchovies in the oil until completely dissolved before adding anything else, and dissolve saffron in warm water for at least 5 minutes before using

attrs.symptom: Breadcrumbs are soggy on the plate
attrs.cause: They were added to the sauce rather than scattered on top at serving
attrs.fix: Toast breadcrumbs separately and add them only at the moment of serving, never into the warm sauce

content.text: Pasta con le Sarde is sold from market stalls in Palermo and cooked at home across Sicily for Sunday lunches. Every cook has a slightly different version. Arguments about the right pasta shape are taken seriously. Fresh sardines are best in spring and early summer. Most good fishmongers stock them from May onwards.
